headline: Coffeehouses Helped Build London’s Scientific Network
lede: A historical event study traces what happened after London neighborhoods opened their first coffeehouses. The authors find lasting growth in mathematical practitioners and instrument shops, especially where university ties were weak, while noting the limits of the records and causal design.

headline: A Course for Making Almost Anything
lede: MIT’s fabrication course moves from CAD and version control to embedded systems, machining, networking, and a working final project. It is less a shortcut to mastery than a map of the territory—and a demanding invitation to cross it.

headline: Show HN Launches Summon the Pitch Machines
lede: Post a project publicly and the automated prospectors arrive: 17 unsolicited sales emails in four days. Their scraped titles, repeated offers, and wrong product names turn startup visibility into another inbox-cleaning chore.

headline: uBlock Origin’s Picker Opens a XSS Door
lede: A malicious website could abuse uBlock Origin’s website-driven element picker to install trusted, script-injecting filters. Update the Firefox extension; the related uBO Lite issue is less severe, but the boundary failure is the warning.

headline: A Smartwatch Maps the Whole Body
lede: EchoMotion uses a commercial watch’s ultrasonic speaker and microphone to estimate the positions of 12 joints without cameras. The system runs on roughly 12 milliwatts and reaches about 2.4-inch average error after brief calibration.

headline: Qwen4-Max Brings a Million-Token Window
lede: Qwen4-Max is a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with native vision, tool use, and a one-million-token context window. Alibaba positions it for long professional and scientific workflows, while its cost and benchmark claims remain company-reported.

headline: Old Short Links Become New Attack Surfaces
lede: Dormant Bitly endings attached to famous posts, PDFs, emails, and QR codes were re-registered and redirected elsewhere. The episode is a small piece of link history with a current lesson: a URL outlives its publisher unless someone keeps control of it.

headline: Exact Gradients Let CAD Models Learn
lede: The seam differentiates a boundary-representation model without repeatedly rebuilding its Boolean and fillet operations. Its mesh-level gradients enable faster geometry optimization, though topology changes and large parameter moves remain outside the method’s safe envelope.

headline: Nvidia’s Next Product May Be Its Leader
lede: Nvidia’s history is also Jensen Huang’s history: gaming GPUs became CUDA, then AI hardware and integrated data-center systems. The succession question is whether a new chief can keep finding the next market—or merely execute the last one.
pullquote: A founder’s greatest product may be the company that can outgrow him.

headline: Tor Ships a Fix Under Sustained Attack
lede: An ongoing distributed denial-of-service attack is overwhelming relays with client circuits. Tor’s rapid 0.4.9.17 release strengthens relay defenses, including IPv6 handling; operators should upgrade while further mitigations are assessed.
